clue.text: Senior nurse, trade union member?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nurse in charge of a hospital ward
second meaning: union members call one another brother and ...

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the ward's senior nurse also belongs to a union.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a ward sister is a senior nurse, and trade unionists address fellow members as brother or sister.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the British title of a ward's senior nurse and also the comradely form of address for a female union colleague.

clue.text: Gemstone — it has sparkle, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the words are to be pronounced rather than read

parts.note: something with sparkle is afire; 'tis afire, run together, is pronounced like the stone

explanation.surface: A jeweller hears that a stone glitters and names the gem.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'it has sparkle' as 'it's afire', said quickly as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a precious blue stone of the corundum family, so it is a gemstone.

clue.text: Commercial interrupting peaceful piece of music

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: serene means calm, peaceful
a commercial is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: An advert breaks into a calm piece of music on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song or instrumental piece, traditionally sung to a lover under a window.

clue.text: Relaxes during course of striptease show

indicators.note: during the course of the words means somewhere inside their run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A performer unwinds while taking part in a striptease act.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or relax, so 'eases' matches 'relaxes' as a third-person verb.

clue.text: Sign of a sore poet? You may see one holding a dagger

parts.note: a scab forms over a healing sore
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet with a scabby sore turns up somewhere a dagger might be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the wordplay; the definition is the descriptive phrase after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that a blade such as a dagger or sword is kept in.

clue.text: Caught vendor upset with agent in London district

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: upset things are knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
'with' joins the second word of the mixed letters

explanation.surface: A market trader is caught out and upset alongside an agent in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Covent Garden is a central London district, once home to the fruit and vegetable market, now the Royal Opera House.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names an area of central London around its famous piazza and former market.

clue.text: Bet on changes involving a normal Corsican family

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap something up within, so one group goes inside the other
something that changes takes a new form, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
par is the normal standard, as in 'up to par'

explanation.surface: A gambler's bet keeps changing, oddly involving an ordinary family from Corsica.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's family, the Bonapartes, came from Ajaccio on Corsica, so the surname is that of a Corsican family.

clue.text: A plank on a ship?

parts.note: taken as written
a board is a plank of wood

explanation.surface: It sounds like asking about a plank found on a ship, perhaps one to walk.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'on a ship' is not describing the plank but defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard means being on or in a vessel, so the adverb means on a ship.

clue.text: Synopsis to assimilate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a noun, a condensed summary
second meaning: a verb, to absorb food or information

explanation.walkthrough: The noun is stressed on the first syllable and the verb on the second, but they are spelt alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a summary of material, and to digest is to take in and absorb, whether food or ideas.

clue.text: Standard is set by leader of hillside community

parts.note: par is the standard or expected level
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so take only the opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of hillside

explanation.surface: A village on a hillside has its standards set by a local leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the community of a local church district, and in Britain also a small unit of local government.

clue.text: Calm, boy before Goran's first service

parts.note: even means calm and steady, as in an even temper
a son is a boy

indicators.note: the first of a name is its opening letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the name Goran

explanation.surface: A calm boy goes before Goran's first serve, as if at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Goran Ivanisevic, the Wimbledon champion, makes 'service' look like tennis; it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, so it is a church service.

clue.text: Product endorsement? Impressive, we initially utter

parts.note: royal can mean magnificent, splendid, as in a royal welcome

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so the word yields just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of we
arrant means utter, complete, as in arrant nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone with grand ideas pronounces their own approval of a product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb, to speak, but it is the adjective meaning complete. A Royal Warrant lets a supplier to the British royal household display the royal arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A Royal Warrant certifies that a firm supplies the royal household, which acts as a prestigious endorsement of its goods.

clue.text: Crewmen losing? Easily

parts.note: a ship's crewmen are its hands
a team that is losing is down, as in two goals down

explanation.surface: A captain asks whether the crew are losing, and is told they are winning easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning hands down means winning with ease, so the idiom serves as an adverb for easily.

clue.text: Leaves bits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, goes away or separates
second meaning: a plural noun, pieces or components

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage, as if 'leaves bits' were scraps of a plant; it is the verb to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to leave or go separate ways, and parts as a plural noun are pieces of a whole.

clue.text: Author drawn by jockey

parts.note: a jockey is a horse rider
drawn means looking tired and gaunt

explanation.surface: An author's portrait has been drawn by a jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' looks like sketched but means gaunt; the pieces are read in reverse clue order because 'drawn by jockey' places the jockey first. H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Rider Haggard was a Victorian novelist, famed for adventure stories such as She.

clue.text: Reportedly go round with type that's someone to look up to

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: to roll is to go round, turning over and over
a model is a type or version, as of a car

explanation.surface: A person who turns things around with a certain type of character is held up as admirable.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose behaviour others admire and imitate.

clue.text: Quotation in comic paper about one — good piece of humour

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the next pieces
something comic is silly and topsy-turvy, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
G is a common abbreviation for good

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is just its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of humour

explanation.surface: A comic newspaper prints a quotation about someone, a good bit of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic paper' suggests a children's comic, but 'comic' stirs the letters of the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is a short quotation placed at the start of a book or chapter.

clue.text: Darbishire's friend, girl not unknown in G&S

indicators.note: not here means without, so a letter is removed from the name before it

parts.note: Jenny is a girl's name
y is a mathematical unknown, like x
taken as written
the initials of Gilbert and Sullivan, with the ampersand dropped

explanation.surface: A girl appears in a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, linked somehow to Darbishire.
explanation.walkthrough: Jennings and Darbishire are the schoolboy friends in Anthony Buckeridge's comic stories set at a boarding school. G&S suggests the operettas but simply gives its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Jennings books, Darbishire is the hero Jennings's loyal best friend, so Jennings is Darbishire's friend.

clue.text: Florists, advocates of peace?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: people who deal in flowers
second meaning: 1960s hippies who preached peace and love

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful literal reading, hence the question mark; the real phrase means the hippies of the 1960s who handed out flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Flower power hippies promoted peace and love, and florists are literally people of flowers.

clue.text: Greek character — priest entertaining Bachelor of Divinity

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so the one word holds the other

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
BD is the abbreviation of the degree

explanation.surface: A Greek man, a priest, plays host to a newly qualified theology graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person from Greece; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a Greek character.

clue.text: Rules soon to be adopted by Civil Service

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the word goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation of Civil Service
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: New regulations will shortly be taken up by government officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Canons are rules or laws, especially church laws, or accepted principles.

clue.text: Fear evident in Territorial Army

indicators.note: evident in means visible within, so the letters can be seen inside the words

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Fear shows among the part-time soldiers of the British reserve force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was the British army's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is a sudden anxiety or fright at danger, so it means fear.

clue.text: Strange orange-red musical instrument

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the colour's letters, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: An oddly orange-red musical instrument catches the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ, such as a harmonium, is a keyboard instrument sounded by vibrating metal reeds.

clue.text: Ring from abroad about coming over

parts.note: abroad means out and about, away from home

indicators.note: coming over suggests flipping, so this word is read from right to left in a down entry

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A phone ring arrives from overseas about a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a telephone call; it is the outermost ring of an archery target.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery and shooting the outer is the outermost ring of the target, so it is a ring.

clue.text: General behaviour in New York city street

parts.note: broad means general, as in broad terms
a way is a manner of behaving, as in set in one's ways

explanation.surface: Someone describes typical behaviour on a New York street.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway is the famous avenue running through Manhattan, home of New York's theatre district.

clue.text: Trace line of ancestry

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a noun, a slight element
second meaning: a breed or lineage, as of animals or plants

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trace' looks like a verb, as in tracing one's ancestry; it is a noun meaning a small hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is both a faint tendency within something and a line of descent within a species.

clue.text: Sailor, very good on ancient instrument? Perfect

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
so means very, as in so good; the pair reads as one intensifier
the lute is an old plucked string instrument

explanation.surface: A sailor is very good on an old instrument, and his playing is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' is best read as 'so (good)': only SO is needed, the setter's wording being loose here.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means complete and total, so it matches perfect in the sense of utter, as in a perfect stranger.

clue.text: Composer — supporter has original of his manuscript

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: the original of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of his
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: A fan of a composer owns his original manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan of the composer; it is an item of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer of symphonies and the German Requiem.
